plan.p0: A plausible mechanism is edge-directed ray painting: each singleton marker expands inward from its boundary into a 3-cell-wide zigzag/checker band of its own color, while other cells stay unchanged. Right-edge markers produce horizontal 3-row bands; bottom-edge markers produce vertical 3-column bands. Overlaps would require a chosen priority rule, not evidenced here.
plan.p1: A contrasting mechanism is full-span stripe stamping: markers on one edge specify bands that extend across the entire perpendicular dimension, with alternating cells in the two outer rows or columns and the complementary phase in the center. This assumes orientation comes from the common marker edge, rather than from each marker’s individual nearest edge.
plan.p2: Another possibility is a fixed local stencil translated from every marker: apply the observed three-line alternating motif repeatedly along the inward axis, clipping it at the grid boundary. This treats each marker independently and would differ when markers are interior, lie on different edges, or overlap; the observed cases do not determine those choices.
plan.p3: A fourth mechanism is global reconstruction: detect the marked edge, sort markers along it, and generate a periodic colored partition whose stripe centers and phases are anchored by those markers. Repeated colors may merge into one interval rather than remain independent stamps, so inputs with gaps, conflicting phases, or multiple marked edges could produce different results.
